clue.text: Old politician's issue with money monopoliser pocketing a grand

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so the monopoliser holds the grand within

parts.note: a quin is one of five children born together, so one's issue
tin is slang for money
someone who hogs something keeps it to themselves
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A former politician whose offspring married a greedy hoarder who has pocketed a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The G slips inside HOG between O and G, giving HOGG. Quintin Hogg (Lord Hailsham) was a senior Conservative minister and Lord Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintin Hogg was a twentieth-century British Conservative statesman, so he fits a description of a past politician.

clue.text: Much rum lifted a German's scallop

indicators.note: much of something is most but not all of it, so the word loses its end

parts.note: rum means odd, or QUEER, with its last letter dropped

indicators.note: in a down clue something lifted is raised upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Someone has drunk a lot of rum after stealing a German's scallop dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the adjective meaning strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A queenie is the familiar name for the queen scallop, a small edible shellfish.

clue.text: Creeper assumes gold colour

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on board, so the creeper takes the metal inside itself

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A climbing plant turns golden in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy off-white shade named after elephant tusk material.

clue.text: Football shirts maybe getting secure delivery at Old Trafford?

parts.note: shirts are an example of tops, hence maybe
to pin is to fasten securely

explanation.surface: Manchester United shirts are sold safely at their home stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is both Manchester United's football stadium and Lancashire's cricket ground, so football leads the eye away from the bowling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward rotation a bowler can put on the ball, so a kind of delivery at a cricket ground.

clue.text: Dissident husband probing drinks and meals

parts.note: a dissident is a no, someone voting against

indicators.note: a probe goes inside what it examines, so the husband pushes into the drinks

parts.note: sups are small mouthfuls of drink
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A rebellious husband snoops into the household's drinking and dining.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is British slang for a big, hearty meal, so the plural fits meals.

clue.text: Handler of frame and poster uncovered old trail

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the word are taken off

parts.note: poster without its first and last letters
O is the abbreviation for old
a path is a trail

explanation.surface: Someone framing an old poster of a hiking route.
explanation.walkthrough: The frame here is the body's skeleton, not a picture frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats the bones and joints by manipulating them, so works on the body's skeletal frame.

clue.text: Plant dope on opponent switching sides

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the first part comes first
the word's two halves trade places, left side going to the right

parts.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope
an anti is someone opposed

explanation.surface: A defector is given inside information on a rival plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope means information here, not a drug; ANTI splits as AN and TI, which swap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentian is a flowering alpine plant famed for its deep blue trumpet blooms.

clue.text: Welsh person possibly disheartened elder stooge

indicators.note: possibly marks the Welsh person as an example, a common surname standing for any Welshman
losing heart means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: JONES, the classic Welsh surname, with its middle letter N taken out
an OAP is an old age pensioner

explanation.surface: A dispirited old Welshman has become someone's dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is British slang for an ordinary person who gets landed with the dull jobs, a dupe or fall guy.

clue.text: Ascetic diocese again reported consort

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the answer matches the spoken sound

parts.note: a Jain follows an ascetic Indian religion
a see is a bishop's diocese; more as in once more

explanation.surface: An austere bishop's diocese is said to have taken a partner again.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, JAIN SEE MORE sounds like the name of Henry VIII's third wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Seymour was Henry VIII's third queen, the wife of a reigning monarch, hence a consort.

clue.text: Black garlic, in a tasting, somewhat repellent

indicators.note: something repellent drives things back, so the run is read backwards
somewhat means only part of something, so the letters are a run inside the phrase

parts.note: a run of letters across garlic, in, a and tasting

explanation.surface: Black garlic offered at a tasting proves rather off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: Black garlic is a real fermented delicacy, which makes Black look like part of the food rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Black in the sense of evil or devilish, as in black magic, matches satanic.

clue.text: Actress and film-maker introducing cleaner international cut

indicators.note: to introduce someone is to come before them, so the film-maker leads

parts.note: James Cameron, director of Titanic and Avatar

indicators.note: the cleaner is cut into by the international, which is placed inside it

parts.note: Daz is a British brand of washing powder
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A star and a director present a global edit of a film about a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: Daz is a washing-powder brand familiar from British TV adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron Diaz is the American film star of There's Something About Mary and Charlie's Angels.

clue.text: Tony, half wasted, pinching boozer's mug

indicators.note: half the word is wasted, thrown away, leaving its other half
to pinch is to grip between two parts, so the remnant holds the boozer

parts.note: the second half of Tony
a boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn

explanation.surface: Tony, half drunk, steals a fellow drinker's beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer looks like a drinker, but in British slang it is the pub itself; 's here is 'is', so the boozer is what gets pinched.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is a gullible fool, and a ninny is a silly, foolish person.

clue.text: Element somewhere in Bedfordshire dividing unopened drug

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening, so the first letter goes
to divide something is to come between its parts, so the town splits the drug

parts.note: opium without its first letter
Luton is a large town in the English county of Bedfordshire

explanation.surface: A dangerous substance is found in a Bedfordshire town, splitting off from a drugs haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonium is a radioactive chemical element, number 94, used in nuclear weapons and reactors.

clue.text: Tense second over in cricket practice when rejecting headgear

indicators.note: in places the three abbreviations inside the practice area
rejecting means throwing back, so the practice word runs backwards

parts.note: cricketers practise in the nets
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
S is the abbreviation for second
O is the scoring abbreviation for an over in cricket

explanation.surface: A nervous cricketer at net practice takes off his hat for another over.
explanation.walkthrough: Only NETS is turned round; T, S and O go into it in their own order.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the broad-brimmed felt cowboy hat, a piece of headgear.

clue.text: Excavation area thus containing roofless meat house

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the meat loses its first letter
containing means holding within, so thus wraps around what follows

parts.note: so means thus
mutton without its top letter
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A dig site is thereby holding a ruined slaughterhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton Hoo in Suffolk is the site where an Anglo-Saxon ship burial was excavated in 1939.

clue.text: Yank with this small basket renouncing head of Iceland

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: renouncing means giving something up, so the basket drops a letter

parts.note: a pannier is a basket, often one of a pair slung on a bike or animal

indicators.note: 'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'Iceland'

parts.note: the first letter of Iceland, the letter given up

explanation.surface: An American with a little basket gives up on leading Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: Yank looks like an American, but here it is a verb, to wrench, and this is the tool you do it with.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is the British word for a wrench, the tool used to tug or wrench nuts round.

clue.text: Unknown German eight occasionally riled mariner

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
acht is German for eight

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of riled

explanation.surface: An anonymous German rowing eight sometimes annoyed a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight looks like a rowing crew, but it is just the number, in German.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtie is an informal, chiefly Australian word for a yachtsman, a kind of sailor or mariner.

clue.text: Restraining, with force, one copper principally finds no good?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of finds
F is the physics symbol for force
I is the Roman numeral one
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A police officer handcuffs a suspect by force and finds it no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper and its principal F lead; force and one follow, then no good closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuffing someone means putting handcuffs on them, physically restraining them.

clue.text: Prevalent Scotch label collectable at peak

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to put an end to it
EMI is a well-known record label

indicators.note: in a down clue the peak is the top, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of collectable

explanation.surface: A collectable whisky label is at the height of its popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky but is the verb meaning to stop or quash.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic means regularly found or widespread in a place or population, so prevalent.

clue.text: Cut beef around morning perhaps cold

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the complaint wraps round the greeting and cold

parts.note: to beef is to complain, to moan
'Morning!' is an example of a greeting, like hi
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut of beef, perhaps cold, served around breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut and beef suggest butchery, but cut is a haircut and beef a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a haircut with the sides shaved and a central strip of hair standing up.

clue.text: Bland type of music for nightclub's top dancer

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one thing stands in for another

parts.note: MOR is middle-of-the-road, unadventurous easy-listening music
a disco is a nightclub
the top letter of the nightclub, which is replaced

explanation.surface: Easy-listening music replaces the nightclub's top dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: Disco's top is its first letter, which the bland music replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A morisco is a Moorish dance, akin to the morris dance, or a performer of it.

clue.text: Slot in this company file

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
an inbox, or in-tray, is where papers are filed for attention

explanation.surface: Put this into the company's records.
explanation.walkthrough: Slot in reads as file away, but it is the coins you slot into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin box is a receptacle with a slot, as on a payphone or meter, into which coins are pushed.

clue.text: One discards, given change of direction, mountain bike?

indicators.note: one direction letter is changed for the other, left for right

parts.note: someone who offloads gets rid of things
R for right replaces L for left

explanation.surface: A rider who changes direction drops a mountain bike.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a mountain bike as one example of a vehicle built for rough terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-roader is any vehicle made for rough terrain, and a mountain bike is one such.

clue.text: Island in middle of this land

indicators.note: in places the island inside the other piece
middle of means only the central letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this
an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: An island lies at the centre of this country.
explanation.walkthrough: Island looks like the definition, which Haiti fits, but land is the definition and the island is AIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation, a country, so it is a land.

clue.text: Part of 13 Down hard, answer causing commotion

parts.note: the last word of the excavation site at 13 Down
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A hard question about the dig site stirs up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is an informal word for a fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Kentish community pelt poor player

parts.note: to pelt is to rain hard
a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor

explanation.surface: A Kent village pelts a bad sportsman with missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Player is an actor here, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainham is a town in Kent, near Gillingham in the Medway area of south-east England.

clue.text: Mum and I felt that affair represents world of TV etc

parts.note: mum's the word: keep quiet, sh
ow is what you say when something hurts
biz is slang for business, an affair

explanation.surface: A mother confesses that a romantic affair stood for the television world.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum is not a mother but the word for silence, and affair means business, not romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Showbiz is short for show business, the entertainment industry including television, film and theatre.

clue.text: London club hurt by wag

parts.note: the Groucho Club is a private members' club in Soho, London
to mar is to spoil or damage
x is the times sign, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A London nightspot is upset by a joker among its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx was the American comedian famed for one-liners, so a wit or wag.
